title: PHASE A FOR A SPACE CIRCULAR ECONOMY MISSION - EXPRO PLUS
description: ESA is encouraging the implementation of a circular economy' in space that ensures long-term orbital sustainability through in-orbit servicing. Several activities comprise the circular economy in space, namely on-orbit assembly, on-orbit manufacturing, and on-orbit recycling, all supported by technologies for on-orbit servicing, rendezvous, and close-proximity operations. These technologies will allow us to treat orbital space as a finite resource, re-use space assets, and minimize the waste associated with building and disposing of spacecraft.ESA concluded a studies campaign in early 2025, which supported four pre-Phase A industrial feasibility studies looking at on-orbit refurbishment, manufacturing, and recycling in Earth orbit. From these studies, two concepts have been selected as winners of the campaign and their concepts have been consolidated together with ESA experts by performing Concurrent Design studies at ESA ESTEC Concurrent Design Facility. As outcome of this work, ESA has identified on-orbit refurbishment as its primary near-term goal for the next generation of circular economy activities through in-orbit servicing capabilities. The scope of the proposed work will be to mature the on-orbit refurbishment concept with a Phase A study focusing on the design of an in-orbit demonstration missions and the identification of the critical technologies to be developed in the next coming years.The procurement will be open competition to all industrial entities, ensuring an opencompetitive approach preparing further steps. Parallel contracts may be placed in case of competitive complementary proposals.

title: Denmark – Construction work – Invitation to M5 Metro Line - Information Meeting
description: Dear potential tenderer Metroselskabet is inviting you to participate in an information meeting with potential interested contractors with interest in the construction of the new M5 metro line in Copenhagen. We are pleased to inform you that The Government and The City of Copenhagen have just reached an political agreement to construct the new M5 Metro Line project in Copenhagen, with nine stations between Copenhagen Central Station and Lynetteholm across Amager. The line is expected to open in two stages in 2036 and 2045 respectively. The goal of M5 is to provide efficient public transport to both existing urban areas that currently do not have metro service (on Amager), as well as new urban development areas, including in the East Harbour (Kløverparken, Refshaleøen and Lynetteholm). The M5 will also add an extra connection across the harbour. The new line will be approx. 15.7 km long standalone metro line with up to 9 stations in total, some underground and some elevated. Some stations and part of the line will be underground in existing dense city environment, and some will be in new city districts that are not yet developed. The first stage is expected to be approx. 6 km. bored twin tunnel with 5 underground stations, approx. 2 km viaducts and 1 elevated station. For the Civil works the project includes construction of tunnels, underground stations and shafts, mechanical and electrical works, elevated sections and stations, ramps, architectural finishes etc. For the transportation system the project includes rolling stock, scada, signalling, passenger information system, power supply, control and maintenance center etc. The first stage is expected to be inaugurated in 2036. Following the adoption of the construction act Metroselskabet expects the procurement process to start in 2026. The second stage is assumed to be inaugurated in 2045 and will be procured in separate contracts. Metroselskabet has set the following 4 project goals for the project: • Reduce the use of resources and climate impact: Metroselskabet has an ambition to reduce the carbon footprint from future metro lines with 50% compared to the existing metro. • Improve passenger experience and operational robustness. It is important to make the public transport system, including the metro, as attractive to people as possible to increase usage. As part of that, operational robustness and reliable service are essential. Not only does a good public transport network provide better mobility solutions in the city but greater use reduces the ’invested CO2’ per passenger km and therefore also a key aspect of sustainability. • Improve safety and the working environment Everyone should be able to work without accidents or injuries, both in construction and operations of the new metro line. • A contribution to the city. A new Metro line should physically meet and connect with the city in a way that creates urban space quality and leave space for increased urban biodiversity. At the market dialogue Metroselskabet would like to discuss the following topics. In light of this development, we would like to invite you to a 30-minute information meeting to discuss the forthcoming process. This session will be conducted via Microsoft Teams and is scheduled for 29th of April at 2:30PM-3:00PM . Please note that this will be a group meeting; individual sessions will be arranged at a later stage as the project progresses. To confirm your participation and receive the Teams meeting link, kindly inform [VIJ@m.dk & NKM@m.dk]. We look forward to your attendance and to share more details about the M5 Metro Line project. Kind Regards, Metroselskabet I/S

title: ECLS Valves I-HAB  Venting and Shut/Off valves (VSOV)
description:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025
 The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada
 The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration
 The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly
 It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the Contractors for the ECLS Venting and Shut/Off Valves for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices
The venting and Shut/Off Valve (VSOV) is part of the equipment belonging to the I-HAB Gateway module
 The Venting Shut-Off Valves (VSOV) is a motorized valve used to vent gas to vacuum
 The VSOV includes a manual override and a visual and an electrical position indication
 A non-propulsive venting section is mounted externally on the primary structure
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered
Further information concerning I-HAB can be found on the Agencys website here:https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon
